# Exquisite Corpse

A Skill Harbor house build: Exquisite Corpse, the blind collective writing game, refereed by your own Muse inside a group chat you own. Each player writes one segment of a sentence without ever seeing what the others write: the referee assigns the segment types in secret (a character, an action, a place, a moment, an ending), collects every segment in a private one-to-one message, seals it away, and only at the deadline assembles the pieces in order and publishes the complete text, all at once. Nobody planned the result, and that collision is the whole game: pieces written blind that, put end to end, tell something stranger and funnier than anyone would have written alone.

The blindness is enforced by the mechanic, not just promised. Contributions never travel in the group thread, the referee never reads, quotes, or even hints at a segment before publication, and the only updates anyone sees are counts without content. Each segment is capped at 15 words and is judged by nobody: there is no right answer and no scoring of quality in the base game, it is pure collective fun. A player who stays silent simply leaves a gap: the published text marks the missing segment in brackets, in its place, and the referee never invents, completes, or repairs a segment for anyone.
